author: adversarial review fix (synced_reader plan, Task 7 follow-up)
summary: Removed useChapterTiming.ts's cross-mount cache. It stored `{groups, audioDurationMs}` keyed only by `${projectId}:${chapterId}` with no invalidation, so a chapter re-rendered mid-session (new sidecar, new audio_generated_at) kept serving the earlier-fetched stale groups to any later remount for the same chapter, silently bypassing the backend timing route's own staleness 404. Investigated for an existing render-completion invalidation signal to reuse (per the original task's flagged note and 03-reader-frontend.md's "invalidate on the same signal..." line) and found none: the peaks sidecar (PlayerBar.tsx) — the closest analog — also has no cross-mount cache, it just refetches whenever its own effect deps change; queue_item_invalidated/project_invalidated are queue-list signals, not render-completion events. Removing the cache (always fetch fresh on mount) matches that existing, already-accepted pattern rather than inventing a new invalidation mechanism.

changes.change: Removed the module-scoped `cache` Map and `cacheKey` helper; the hook now always issues a fresh fetch on mount/dep-change (chapterId, projectId), matching useRenderGroups.ts/useChapterAnalysis.ts's existing no-cross-mount-cache pattern. Behavior for 404/network-failure/200 cases is unchanged.

Replaced the 'does not refetch on remount once cached' test (which encoded the buggy contract) with a regression test: two sequential mounts of the same (projectId, chapterId) with different mocked fetch responses (simulating a re-render between mounts) must both hit the network and the second mount must reflect the fresh data, not the first mount's stale result. TDD-verified: this test fails against the pre-fix code (returns stale audioDurationMs 6360 instead of fresh 9000), passes after the fix.

invariants: useChapterTiming has no persistent cache across mounts/unmounts; every mount for a given (chapterId, projectId) re-fetches the timing route. The backend route's own audio_generated_at staleness check (Task 5) remains the sole authority on whether a sidecar is usable — the frontend no longer has a cache layer that could disagree with it.
note: Follow-up to the 2026-07-17-synced-reader-task07-frontend-sync-engine.json entry, which explicitly flagged the missing invalidation signal as out of scope. This fix resolves it by removing the cache rather than building a bespoke invalidation signal, since no equivalent exists elsewhere in the frontend to reuse.
